title: Surface-pinned nonsingular topologically charged defects in nanoplasmonics
authors: Michael I. Tribelsky, Vladimir V. Ternovski
abstract: We discuss surface-pinned, topologically charged, nonsingular defects (SD) in light scattering by a plasmonic object. They follow from exact Maxwell boundary conditions and are purely topological---unaffected by surface forces. At optical frequencies, in (quasi) 2D, they appear in the electric and Poynting vector fields for $H^{(z)}$ polarization, not for $E^{(z)}$. Exact solutions for a circular cylinder reveal topological charge-conserving bifurcations involving SDs with bulk singularities or SDs alone, and contraction of defect regions under loss.
summary: This theoretical work characterizes surface-pinned, topologically charged defects in light scattering from plasmonic nanostructures. The defects are purely topological, arising from boundary conditions, and their existence is confirmed through charge-conserving bifurcations. The study highlights that these defects are robust features of the electromagnetic field structure, independent of surface energy models.
main_problem: The paper investigates the existence and properties of surface-pinned, topologically charged, nonsingular defects (SDs) that arise in light scattering from plasmonic objects.
main_result: These defects are purely topological, dictated by Maxwell boundary conditions, and are found in the electric and Poynting vector fields for H(z) polarization, demonstrating topological charge conservation during field bifurcations.
method: The analysis uses exact solutions for light scattering (e.g., for a cylinder) and defines the topological charge via the winding number calculated from one-sided traces of the field components at the material interface.
model_or_system: The study models light scattering from a plasmonic object, specifically analyzed in (quasi) 2D at optical frequencies, using the framework of Maxwell's equations.
key_observables: The local and global winding numbers ($w_E, w_S$), the field patterns in the E and Poynting vector fields, and the evolution of defect domains in parameter space.
important_parameters: Optical frequencies, dissipation ($\varepsilon''$), and the material permittivity ($\varepsilon'$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is simplified to 2D scattering by an infinite cylinder, and the topological charge is defined by regularizing the sharp boundary interface.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic field lines near an SD, charge-conserving annihilation processes involving bulk saddles and SDs, and maps showing domains of different SD winding numbers in the parameter space.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical basis for SDs from Maxwell's equations, demonstrates their existence and properties using exact solutions (e.g., for a cylinder), analyzes the topological charge conservation through bifurcations, and examines the effect of dissipation on these structures.
why_interesting: The rigorous topological classification of field structures in plasmonics provides a powerful, geometry-independent diagnostic tool for understanding light-matter interactions at interfaces, which has implications for designing advanced optical components.
